items.informal_name: Finite support functions from finite set product
items.type: {ι : Type u_1} → {α : Type u_2} → [inst : Zero α] → Finset ι → (ι → Finset α) → Finset (ι →₀ α)
items.informal_description: Given a finite set $ s $ over a type $ \iota $ and a function $ t $ assigning to each $ i \in s $ a finite set $ t(i) $, this constructs the finite set of all finite support functions $ f : \iota \to_0 \alpha $ such that $ f(i) \in t(i) $ for each $ i \in s $. This is achieved by first forming the dependent product of the $ t(i) $ over $ s $, then applying an injective indicator function that maps these functions to their finite support representations with zero extension outside $ s $.

items.informal_name: Dependent product of finite sets as finite support functions
items.type:
{ι : Type u_1} →
  {α : ι → Type u_2} →
    [DecidableEq ι] → [inst : (i : ι) → Zero (α i)] → Finset ι → ((i : ι) → Finset (α i)) → Finset (Π₀ (i : ι), α i)
items.informal_description: Given a finite set $ s $ over an index type $ \iota $ and a family of finite sets $ t(i) $ for each $ i \in s $, this constructs the finite set of all dependent functions with finite support in $ s $, where each function assigns to $ i \in s $ an element of $ t(i) $ and is zero elsewhere. The result is formed by taking the product of the $ t(i) $ over $ s $ and mapping it to dependent finite support functions via zero extension.

items.informal_name: Cartesian product of a finitely supported family of finite sets
items.type: {ι : Type u_1} → {α : Type u_2} → [inst : Zero α] → (ι →₀ Finset α) → Finset (ι →₀ α)
items.informal_description: Let $f$ be a function from a type $\iota$ to the finite subsets of a type $\alpha$ with finite support (meaning $f(i)$ is the empty set for all but finitely many $i$). The function `Finsupp.pi f` computes the Cartesian product of the sets $f(i)$ over the support of $f$. The result is a finite set of functions $g$ from $\iota$ to $\alpha$ with finite support, where each $g$ is constructed by selecting an element from each non-empty set $f(i)$ for $i$ in the support of $f$, and is zero outside this support.

items.informal_name: Membership in Dependent Finite Support Functions iff Support Subset and Value Conditions
items.informal_description: A dependent finite support function $ f $ belongs to the set $ s.\text{dfinsupp} \, t $ if and only if two conditions hold: (1) the support of $ f $ (the set of indices $ i $ where $ f(i) \neq 0 $) is a subset of $ s $, and (2) for every index $ i \in s $, the value $ f(i) $ lies in the corresponding finite set $ t(i) $.

The construction is formed by taking the product of the $ f(i) $ over the support and mapping it to dependent finite support functions via zero extension.

items.informal_name: Membership Criterion for Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : Zero α] {s : Finset ι} {f : ι →₀ α} {t : ι → Finset α},
  f ∈ s.finsupp t ↔ f.support ⊆ s ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, f i ∈ t i
items.informal_description: A finite support function $ f $ belongs to the set $ s.\text{finsupp} \, t $ if and only if two conditions hold: (1) the support of $ f $ (i.e., the set of indices where $ f $ is non-zero) is contained in the finite set $ s $, and (2) for every index $ i \in s $, the value $ f(i) $ lies in the corresponding finite set $ t(i) $. Symbolically, $ f \in s.\text{finsupp} \, t \iff \text{support}(f) \subseteq s \land (\forall i \in s, f(i) \in t(i)) $.
